findings.title: 【注意喚起】相次ぐ情報漏洩、その原因の一つは「アプリ解析からのサーバ攻撃」― AIで高度化する脆弱性探索、Androidアプリを手がかりにしたA2B攻撃に注意 ―
findings.summary_md: NICT's CYNEX threat intelligence team LETTICE warned on October 13, 2026 that attackers were reverse-engineering publicly available Android applications to discover backend APIs and attack the servers behind them, a technique it calls App-to-Backend (A2B) attacks. Even when the app itself has no vulnerability, weaknesses in backend authentication, authorization, or input validation can lead to unauthorized access and personal data leaks. NICT noted that AI can make app analysis and vulnerability discovery more efficient, potentially extending these attacks to more systems. The alert links to a PDF containing attack details, targeted weaknesses, countermeasures, and IoCs.

findings.title: Chinese AI tool used in cyberattacks on Japanese companies, investigation finds
findings.summary_md: The Japan Times reported on October 20, 2026 that GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae, a subsidiary of GMO Internet Group, announced it had detected use of a Chinese-developed AI tool called Artex in attacks targeting Japanese companies, based on forensic logs. GMO linked the same tool to a rash of breaches at South Korean financial organizations reported earlier in the month by CrowdStrike. A Teikoku Databank survey cited in the article said around one-sixth of Japanese companies had suffered breaches. The announcement preceded the broader October surge disclosures by several weeks.

findings.title: Recent AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks in Japan: Investigating Attack Infrastructure and Techniques
findings.summary_md: JPCERT/CC published on October 21, 2026 the results of its investigation into infrastructure used in a series of unauthorized access incidents reported by multiple Japanese organizations. It confirmed attackers used AI to scan for known vulnerabilities and carry out attacks via APIs, and found they analyzed Android application packages to identify API endpoints and test them for server-side request forgery. On another server, investigators found APK files plus Blutter and jadx, tools for reverse-engineering Flutter and Android applications, along with apk_extract directories and extracted string files. JPCERT/CC also found evidence of EDR evasion, web shells, and attacks against MySQL, Jenkins, and email gateways, and noted some targeted services outside Japan.

findings.title: Behind Japan’s Warnings of a Cyber Crisis
findings.summary_md: Recorded Future's Insikt Group reported on October 22, 2026 that reported cyberattacks against Japanese organizations rose 48 percent between Q2 and Q3 2026, from 621 to 918, according to its Intelligence Platform. Trend Micro similarly noted attacks against Japan from January through September 2026 exceeded the total for all of 2025, with 86 attacks reported by Japanese companies in September alone. The post details Q3 breaches including an October 7 ransomware incident at cloud provider IDCFrontier affecting 495 companies and local governments, and an October 13 misuse of a Sourcenext member information retrieval API that exposed 22,519,960 customer records. It attributes part of the exposure to legacy systems, noting over 60 percent of Japanese firms still use end-of-life software according to an April 2026 Money Forward article.

findings.title: Japan’s Cyberattack Surge Tests Its Push to Strengthen Defenses
findings.summary_md: Insurance Journal reported on October 30, 2026 that Japan was facing an intense wave of AI-powered cyberattacks, with dozens of incidents affecting companies from brokerages to delivery firms. TrendAI vice president Tom Kellermann attributed many attacks to Russian-speaking groups such as LockBit and Qilin and said AI agents and open-source hacking tools lowered barriers against Japan's outdated infrastructure. Daiki Fukumori of GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae linked the Chinese-developed ARTEX tool to many recent attacks, and Yutaka Sejiyama of Macnica said at least 81 incidents had been reported since July, nearly a third of attacks in the last three years. The article also noted Japan's PHP exposure and emergency patching by firms such as Mizuho Financial Group.

findings.title: Cyberattacks Are Skyrocketing in Japan as Researchers Trace AI-Assisted Intrusions
findings.summary_md: Socket published on November 12, 2026 a detailed account of Japan's October surge, reporting 233 publicly disclosed security incidents, roughly 2.4 times the previous monthly record, and an MM Research Institute estimate of about 185 million personal information records exposed or potentially exposed. It documented the Arara breach of approximately 81.3 million email addresses affecting up to 380 corporate customers and the Ymir Link Cuenote FC intrusion exposing about 47.9 million records from 49 systems via software exploitation, stolen session information, and CSV export abuse. It also reported Nitori's disclosure of up to 37.62 million customer records on November 9 and Japan's announcement of a 10 billion yen emergency cybersecurity package. Socket noted PHP runs on about 92 percent of Japan-hosted sites and that exploitation of recent critical PHP flaws began before their October 21 public disclosure.
